evals.prompt: I need to write widget tests for a new DSButton atom with variants (primary, secondary, ghost), states (default, loading, disabled), and an onPressed callback. What are the required test sections and what patterns should I follow?
evals.expected_output: Lists 6 required sections: basic rendering, states, variants, interactions, defaults, accessibility. Uses pumpApp helper. AAA pattern. Names follow 'should [verb] when [condition]'. Variant loop pattern. Disabled state verifies callback not invoked.

assertions.text: Response covers all 6 required test sections: basic rendering, states, variants, interactions, defaults, accessibility
Response uses pumpApp helper (not pumpWidget directly) to mount widgets
Response shows the disabled state test verifying that the callback is NOT invoked when tapped

evals.prompt: How do I efficiently test all 3 variants of my DSButton without writing 3 separate copy-paste tests?
evals.expected_output: Shows the variant loop pattern: for (final variant in DSButtonVariant.values) { testWidgets('should render ${variant.name}', ...) }. Explains test independence — each test stands alone.

assertions.text: Response uses a for loop over WidgetVariant.values to iterate all variants
Response keeps each test independent — no shared mutable state between iterations

evals.prompt: My DSButton test is crashing when I pass null for the onPressed callback. How should I write a null-safety test to verify it doesn't crash?
evals.expected_output: Shows testWidgets with null onPressed, calls pumpApp with widget, taps widget, asserts no exception thrown. Explains that null callbacks must not crash — test passes if no exception.

assertions.text: Response shows a test that pumps the widget with onPressed: null (not provided or explicitly null)
Response taps the widget and verifies no exception is thrown — passing without an exception is the success condition
Response follows the 'should not crash when callback is null' naming convention
